fixes.row: Joy from the LORD: given by God, in His presence, in His word (and verb row: Rejoice in the LORD, in God, in the Lord; before Him...)
fixes.why: Rule 3, picked by hand. The verse says only 'You have enlarged the nation... rejoice before You'. Isaiah 9:1-2 use 'He' and name no one; the nearest naming is 8:17 behind an intervening passage, the next is 9:7. Unlike the Psalms picks, no naming of the LORD sits close enough to make 'You' clear. The verse still stands in 'Joy and salvation, rescue, victory' and 'Joy at feasts' (harvest).
fixes.fix: Remove Isa.9.3 from the pick lists of 'Joy from the LORD...' and of the verb row 'Rejoice in the LORD, in God, in the Lord; before Him...'; keep it in the salvation/victory and feasts rows.

fixes.row: Joy from the LORD: given by God, in His presence, in His word
fixes.why: These are the rocky-ground hearers who receive the word with joy and fall away, the proof-texts in the Reformed/Wesleyan quarrel over perseverance. Filed under a heading that says the joy is from the LORD, the page seems to settle whether that joy was God's gift (rule 2). The verses say only that the hearer receives the word with joy.
fixes.fix: Move Mark.4.16 and Matt.13.20 to 'Every other use of the joy nouns'; Luke.8.13 is already in 'Joy and sorrow' and 'Joy beside... faith', so drop it from this row too.

fixes.row: Joy from the LORD: given by God, in His presence, in His word
fixes.why: The label says 'Joy from the LORD' (a decision: He gives it), while the row's own note says the page does not choose between the joy He has and the joy He gives (Neh 8:10 'the joy of the LORD'). Label and note disagree, and the lead example is the ambiguous one.
fixes.fix: Relabel to 'The joy of the LORD, and joy God gives: in His presence, in His word', keeping the note.

fixes.row: Joy in heaven over one sinner who repents; “Enter into the joy of your master”; joy and the kingdom
fixes.why: The merge puts three unrelated sayings under one heading and one note: joy in heaven over repentance (Luke 15), the master's joy (Matt 25, whose joy is not stated), and the kingdom (Matt 13:44 is a man's joy at treasure; Rom 14:17 is joy in the Holy Spirit, which has its own row). One heading invites reading them as one idea, and the repentance note covers only two of the six verses. The four examples shown (Luke 15:7, 15:10, Matt 25:21, 25:23) never show the 'kingdom' part of the label (rule 6).
fixes.fix: Split: 'Joy in heaven over one sinner who repents' (Luke 15:7, 15:10; keep the no-side note on repentance) and 'Enter into the joy of your master; joy and the kingdom' (Matt 25:21, 25:23, Matt 13:44, Rom 14:17; note: whose joy the master's is, the page does not decide). If kept as one row, set lead to Luke.15.7, Matt.25.21, Matt.13.44, Rom.14.17.

fixes.why: Rules 3 and 1. In Zech 4:10 it is 'these seven eyes of the LORD' that rejoice at the plumb line in Zerubbabel's hand, a figure; the LORD is not the stated rejoicer. Filing it under 'The LORD rejoices' assigns the joy to Him by inference. It is already in 'Rejoice at what they see or hear'.
fixes.fix: Remove Zech.4.10 from 'The LORD rejoices, delights' (7 verses remain: Zeph 3:17, Isa 62:5, 65:19, Jer 32:41, Deut 30:9, 28:63, Ps 104:31).

fixes.why: Keeping the verse is right. The note says the same verb 'speaks of the LORD's pleasure in destroying', which is true but is half the verse and drops its setting. Deut 28:63 reads 'Just as it pleased the LORD to make you prosper and multiply, so also it will please Him to annihilate you', in the curses for breaking the covenant. The short note neither softens nor adds, but it reads harsher than the verse and gives none of the context the text itself supplies.
fixes.fix: Note: 'Deut 28:63, among the covenant curses, sets the LORD's pleasure in making Israel prosper beside His pleasure in destroying them if they break the covenant; kept as the text has it.'

fixes.row: The LORD makes glad: made them glad; asked to make us glad
fixes.why: Rule 6: none of the four examples (Ezra 6:22, 2 Chr 20:27, Neh 12:43, Isa 56:7) is a request, so the 'asked to make us glad' half of the label is not shown.
fixes.fix: Set lead to Ezra.6.22, 2Chr.20.27, Ps.90.15, Isa.56.7 (or Ps.86.4).

fixes.row: Told to rejoice, and told not to
fixes.why: Rule 5. The Torah's repeated 'you shall rejoice before the LORD' at the feasts is the largest body of commanded joy in the Hebrew Scriptures, but the stance rule did not take it, so the row's commands come from the Psalms, the prophets and the apostles only (Phil 4:4 and 1 Thess 5:16 are two of its four examples). A reader would take it as the whole of what Scripture commands about rejoicing. These verses sit only in 'Rejoice in the LORD... before Him' and 'Rejoicing together'.
fixes.fix: Add the verses above (`add`) to 'Told to rejoice, and told not to', and set lead so a Torah command shows, e.g. Ps.32.11, Deut.16.11, Phil.4.4, Hos.9.1.

fixes.row: Told to rejoice, and told not to
fixes.why: Luke 12:19 is the rich fool talking to himself ('Eat, drink, and be merry'), not a command anyone gives; set beside Phil 4:4 under 'Told to rejoice' it reads as an instruction. Separately, the row puts 'Rejoice always' next to 'Do not rejoice' with no word on what each is about, and a reader may take it for a contradiction: the prohibitions concern an enemy's fall (Prov 24:17, Obad 12, Mic 7:8), the nations' way (Hos 9:1), the spirits' submission (Luke 10:20), the Philistines' relief (Isa 14:29).
fixes.fix: Remove Luke.12.19 (it stays in 'Everyday joy'). Add note: 'The commands and the prohibitions each name what to rejoice in or not; the prohibitions are about particular joys (an enemy's fall, Prov 24:17, Obad 12), not about joy as such.'

fixes.row: Rejoice in trials and sorrow: suffering, persecution; rejoice and weep
fixes.why: Rule 1. The union of grief words took verses that do not say anyone rejoices in trial: Lam 1:21 is the enemies glad at the speaker's trouble; Hos 10:5 mourners over an idol 'who rejoiced in its glory'; Prov 10:1 and 17:21 a wise son's joy against a foolish son's grief; Prov 29:2 people rejoice when the righteous flourish and groan when the wicked rule. Under this heading they read as the text telling the sufferer to be glad, which the suffering reader and the justice-minded one will object to; Lam 1:21 in particular is rejoicing at another's pain. All five have a better home elsewhere (fall row, Everyday joy, Rejoicing together).
fixes.fix: Remove Lam.1.21, Hos.10.5, Prov.10.1, Prov.17.21, Prov.29.2 from this row; consider relabelling it descriptively: 'Rejoicing in suffering and persecution; rejoicing and weeping together'.

fixes.row: Everyday joy: one's work and youth, a wife, a son; what makes glad (wine, oil, a good word); making merry at a feast
fixes.why: The label reads as ordinary approved joys, but the row also holds the rich fool's merriment, the rich man's 'joyous splendor' before Lazarus, the wicked who prosper (Job 21:12), and Rev 11:10, where the earth-dwellers gloat and send gifts over the killed witnesses. That last is no everyday joy and is already in the fall row.
fixes.fix: Remove Rev.11.10 from this row. Add note: 'Includes merry-making the text sets against itself or against its makers (Luke 12:19, 16:19, Job 21:12); the label names only what is done.' Also set the fourth lead to Luke.15.23 so 'making merry at a feast' is shown (rule 6).

fixes.row: Every other use: rejoice, be glad, exult
fixes.why: Rule 1 and the original-arbitrates rule. John 5:35 (ἀγαλλιάω) and Prov 13:9 (שָׂמַח) really use the ordinary 'rejoice' words that the Berean rewords, and are rightly kept with the note. Job 3:6 is not secure: most translations and commentators read the verb as 'be joined' (a night not joined to the days of the year), the Berean has no joy word, and the worker's own report admits doubt. A curse on the night in a hub of joy, on a minority parse, would mislead. The note also uses the unexplained word 'MACULA'.
fixes.fix: Add Job.3.6 to `sense_drop`. Rewrite the note: 'In John 5:35 and Prov 13:9 the Greek and Hebrew words are the ordinary ones for "rejoice", which the Berean renders otherwise ("bask", "shines brightly").'

fixes.row: Joy and sorrow...; Joy and salvation...; Joy with singing... (merged noun rows)
fixes.why: Rule 6, merged rows whose four examples miss a part of the label: 'Joy and sorrow' shows nothing of 'joy taken away, ended' (17 of its 40 verses); 'Joy and salvation, rescue, victory' no 'good news'; 'Joy with singing... at the ark, the sacrifice, the altar' no sacrifice or altar ('Everyday joy' is covered by its own fix).
fixes.fix: lead for 'Joy and sorrow': Jas.1.2, Ps.30.11, John.16.20, Isa.24.8. 'Joy and salvation': Isa.12.3, Isa.35.10, Luke.2.10, 1Kgs.1.40. 'Joy with singing': 1Chr.15.16, 1Chr.15.25, 2Chr.30.21, Luke.24.52, or another verse that names a sacrifice or the altar (2Chr.29.30 is a candidate).

worker_points.point: 1. Divine persons by pick: 'You' in psalms (Ps 4:7, 16:11, 21:6, 30:11, 51:8, 51:12, 92:4; 5:11, 33:21, 40:16, 66:6, 89:16) and the LORD speaking in the first person (Isa 65:19, Jer 32:41)
worker_points.why: Checked each in context: every psalm names the LORD or God in its opening verses or a verse or two before (Ps 4:1,3; 16:1-2; 21:1; 30:1; 51:1,10; 5:1,10,12; 33:1; 40:1,13; 66:1; 89:15 right before v16), and these are hand picks, not inferred rules. Isa 65:19 and Jer 32:41 are named in the same speech. The one place the naming is not close is Isa 9:3 (see fixes). The other 'You' picks may stay.

worker_points.point: 2. Deut 28:63 in 'The LORD rejoices, delights' with its note
worker_points.why: Hard verse rightly kept and the note neither softens nor sensationalises, but it leaves out the verse's own 'just as ... so also' and the covenant setting; fix is a fuller note (see fixes).

worker_points.point: 3. 'Rejoice in the Lord' (Phil 3:1, 4:4, 4:10) and 'Jesus rejoiced' (Luke 10:21, John 11:15)
worker_points.why: The note names the κύριος and says readers take it of Christ or the Father without choosing. Luke 10:21 names Jesus and John 11:15 is Jesus speaking.

worker_points.point: 4. Joy and the Holy Spirit (Gal 5:22, Rom 14:17, 15:13, 1 Thess 1:6, Acts 13:52)
worker_points.why: Each verse names the Spirit or the fruit of the Spirit with joy; the note says no more.

worker_points.point: 5. Luke 15 rows, repentance, and the merged 'Enter into the joy of your master' / kingdom row
worker_points.why: The verb row 'Rejoice over what was lost and found' is fine with its note. The noun merge puts three different sayings under one heading and one note, and its examples do not show the kingdom part (see fixes: split or re-lead).

worker_points.point: 6. Joy from the LORD carrying 'the joy of the LORD'
worker_points.why: The label chooses 'from' while the note refuses to choose; relabel (see fixes). Also move the rocky-ground verses out.

worker_points.point: 7. Rejoicing over another's fall or ruin, at judgment; in wealth, an idol
worker_points.why: The row sets forbidden gloating (Prov 24:17, Obad 12), reported gloating (Ps 35, Lam 2:17), prayed-against gloating, and the righteous rejoicing at God's judgment (Ps 58:10, 97:8, Rev 18:20) side by side, and the note says it takes no side. A rabbi and a justice-minded reader can accept this: it is the text, hard verses included. The semicolon splits the label into its parts; the wealth/idol group is a different object but is named in the label.

worker_points.point: 8. Joy and sorrow (Jas 1:2, 1 Pet 4:13); must not read as telling the suffering to be glad
worker_points.why: The noun row 'Joy and sorrow' is fine, since 'and' is neutral. The verb row 'Rejoice in trials and sorrow' is not: it sounds imperative and holds five verses that do not rejoice in trial (see fixes).

worker_points.point: 9. Joy beside peace, love, hope and faith
worker_points.why: Set side by side with no ranking. The Old Testament verses in it carry the actual words (שָׁלוֹם, תִּקְוָה, מָלֵא), so they are not filed under a New Testament heading as if they belonged there; Isa 55:12 and Prov 10:28 are examples of that.

worker_points.point: 10. Joy and salvation, rescue, victory (Judg 16:23, Esth 8-9)
worker_points.why: Joy over defeated enemies is what the verses say; Judg 16:23 is the Philistines' joy credited to Dagon and says so. No tilt. Kept as hard verses.

worker_points.point: 11. Everyday joy / rejoicing in wealth, an idol: unapproved joys beside approved ones
worker_points.why: Descriptive labels are acceptable in the fall/wealth row; in 'Everyday joy' they hide the warning cases and include Rev 11:10 (see fixes).

Labelled by what the verses weigh, 'pleasure and mirth; the righteous and the wicked', not as a verdict on joy; Eccl 9:7 and 5:20 are in 'Joy from the LORD', so the weighing is balanced. Luke 15:7 is its fourth example (the 'righteous ones who do not need to repent' line); it is the text, but Prov 21:15 or Ps 97:11 would be a safer fourth lead, leaving Luke 15:7 to its own row.

worker_points.point: 13. Told to rejoice, and told not to (stance rule, ten exclusions)
worker_points.why: Exclusions are reasoned and fine. The row misses the Torah's festival commands (rule 5) and holds the rich fool's self-address (see fixes). Phil 4:4 beside Prov 24:17 and Obad 12 is fair once a note says what the prohibitions are about.

worker_points.point: 14. Rejoice at what they see or hear; Rejoicing together; Everyday joy: judgement picks
worker_points.why: The Deut 12, 16 and Neh 8 feasts are heard on their own terms: they lead 'Rejoicing together' and 'Rejoice in the LORD... before Him' (Deut 12:7 shown as its own example) and 'Joy at feasts' (Esth 9:19, Jer 7:34, Neh 8:12 shown), the Hebrew first; the New Testament verses follow. Rejoicing together mixes Israel's household rejoicing with Paul's 'I rejoice over you', but the label separates them by semicolons and begins with the Torah household.

worker_points.point: 15. Kept because the original has the joy word (Eccl 4:16, Jonah 4:6, Hos 7:3, Ps 46:4, Job 3:6, John 5:35, Prov 13:9)
worker_points.why: John 5:35 and Prov 13:9 stand with the note. Job 3:6 should go (see fixes). Eccl 4:16, Jonah 4:6, Hos 7:3, Ps 46:4 print 'celebrated', 'pleased', 'delight', 'delight': close enough to a joy sense to need no note.

worker_points.point: Rule 4: ἀγαλλιάω / εὐφραίνω grouped with the Hebrew family as 'the Greek that renders them'
worker_points.why: The 'renders' claim lives only in the spec's underscore notes; the built hub states no equivalence. Each example carries its own word chip, χαίρω's greeting sense is dropped, the different words רָנַן, עָלַז, עָלַץ, εὐφροσύνη are named apart, and no label says the words are one. εὐφραίνω ('to celebrate') sits mostly in the merry-making and command rows, where its sense fits.

missing.what: καυχάομαι, which the Berean renders 'rejoice'/'exult' (Rom 5:2, 5:3, 5:11, Jas 1:9), is neither in the hub nor in the 'others' block, though Rom 5:3 ('we also rejoice in our sufferings') is among the most-sought joy verses. It is a different word ('boast'), so it belongs in 'Other words translated joy, rejoice, exult', named apart, never in the rows.

summary: The joy hub is true to the text in nearly every row, the divine-person psalm picks are close enough, and no row equates different words, but thirteen points need fixing. The chief ones are Isa 9:3 and Zech 4:10 filed as the LORD's by inference, the rocky-ground hearers under 'Joy from the LORD', the merged Luke 15 / master / kingdom row, five verses mislabelled as rejoicing in trial, the Torah's festival commands absent from 'Told to rejoice', and Job 3:6, a doubtful parse that should go.
